FOREWORD

This Indian Standard which is identical with ISO 2448:1998 `Fruits and vegetable products -- Determination of ethanol content' issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of the Processed Fruits and Vegetables Sectional Committee and approval of the Food and Agriculture Division Council. In the adopted standard, certain terminology and conventions Standards. Attention is particularly drawn to the following: a) Wherever the words `International as'lndian Standard'; and are not identical to those used in Indian

Standard' appear referring to this standard, they should be read

b) Comma (,) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards, the current practice is to use a point (.) as the decimal marker. FRUIT AND VEGETABLE PRODUCTS -- DETERMINATION OF ETHANOL CONTENT
1 Scope
This International products. Standard specifies a method for the chemical determination of ethanol in fruit and vegetable

The method is not applicable

to products containing

more than 5 % (m/m)

of ethanol.

In the case of products containing

essential oils, it is necessaty

to remove the latter (see annex A).

2 Definition
For the purposes of this International 2.1 Standard, the following definition applies.

ethanol content mass of the substances determined by the method specified in this International Standard, percentage by mass for solid productsor as grams per 100 ml for liquidproducts

expressed

as a

3 Principle
Separation of the ethanol by distillation, followed by oxidation by potassium bichromate in a sulfuric acid medium. Determination of the excess bichromate by ammonium iron(II) sulfate in the presence of iron(II)-1,1 Ophenanthroline as indicator.

4 Reagents
Use only reagents of recognized water of equivalent purity. 4.1 4.2 4.3 analytical grade, unless otherwise specified, and distilled or demineralized water or

to 1 ml of ammonium 4.6 iron(H) sulfate solution (4.6).

5 Apparatus
Usual laboratory apparatus and, in particular, the following.

5.1

Distillation apparatus, comprising a 500 ml flask surmounted by a fractionation column and a condenser ending in a slightly tapered extension piece long enough to reach to the bottom `of a 100 ml volumetric fkw?k.
Any other steam distillation apparatus may be used, provided that it satisfies the following criterion.

No loss of ethanol greater than 0,02 `?4.shall occur in the course of a distillation; i.e. 200 ml of a 10% (WV) ethanol/water mixture distilled five times in succession shall contain at least 9,9 Y. of ethanol after the last distillation. 5.2 Heating apparatus, which does not cause even slight decomposition the flask. 5.3 5.4 5.5 of the extractable materials contained in

Volumetric flasks, of capacity 100 ml. Pipettes, of capacities 5 ml, 10 ml and 20 ml. Burettes, of capacity 50 ml, fitted with a stopcock.

5.6 Wide-necked flasks, of capacity 250 ml, fitted with ground glass Stormers, clean, drv, free from Cwease and airtight (absolute tightness can be en&red with the aid of a-polytet~afluoreth~ ene sleeve). -" 5.7

Blender. Balance, capable of weighing to the nearest 0,01 g.

6 Sampling
It is important the laboratory during transport or storage. receive a sample which is truly representative and has not been damaged or changed

Sampling is not part of the method specified in this International Standard. As there is no sDecific International Standard dealing with fruit and vegetable products, it is recommended that the parties concerned come to an agreement on the subject.

8 Procedure
It it is required to check whether the repeatability requirement (clause 10) is met, carry out two determinations in NOTE accordance with 8.2.1 to 8.2.3.

8.1 Teat potiion
Weigh, to the nearest 0,01 g, a mass of the prepared sample, or take a voiume of it such that the quantity of ethanol collected in 100 ml of distillate is iess than 1 g,

8.2 Determination 8.2.1 Distillation Dilute the test portion with about 50 ml of water and transfer it quantitatively to the flask of the distillation apparatus (5.1 ). Rinse the vessel used to take the test portion with not more than 120 ml of water, collecting the rinsing water in the flask.
Make the product slightly alkaline (pH 8 + 0,2) with the calcium hydroxide suspension (4.3), shaken before use.

Add glass beads or pieces of porcelain to control the rate of boiling. Pour 10 ml of water into a 100 ml volumetric flask (5.3) and insert the end of the tapered extension of the distillation apparatus so that it is immersed in the liquid. Distil the diluted test portion (previously made alkaline) in such a way that the distillate, volumetric flask, is at a relatively low temperature (15 `C to 20 "C). Collect about 80 ml to 85 ml of distillate. millilitres of water. Shake the volumetric few minutes. Stop the distillation and rinse the condenser when it reaches the

and extension

with a few

flask to mix the contents.

if necessary,

immerse the flask in cold water (15 `C to 20 `C) for a

Dilute the contents of the volumetric 8.2.2

flask to the mark with water and shake.

Oxidation
bichromate solution (4.4), accurately measured (see note), and 20 ml of dilute sulfuric

Pour 20 ml (Vl ) of potassium

acid (4.2) into a 250 ml flask with a ground glass stopper (5.6) and shake. Add 10 ml (Vo) of distillate (8.2.1), accurately measured. Stopper the flask, moistening the stopper with a drop of

sulfuric acid (4. 1). Shake the flask and wait for at least 30 rein, shaking the flask from time to time. The resultant mixture should in no case assume the green coloration of the chromium cation as this would indicate that the ethanol content of the test portion was too high. If this occurs, recommence the oxidation taking a smaller amount of distillate (for example 5 ml). If necessary, recommence both distillation and oxidation taking a smaller test portion. Take account of any such changes in the calculations. If the test portion contains too little ethanol, a smaller amount of potassium bichromate solution (4.4) may be used, i.e. 10 ml or 5 ml of this solution, diluted with 10 ml or 15 ml of distilled water, respectively. Take account of any such change in the calculations.

IS 15096:2002 ISO 2448:1998
8.2.3 Titration

Titrate the excess of bichromate, using the ammonium iron(H) sulfate solution (4.6). The excess of bichromate should be at least equal to 20 % of the quantity used for the blank test, Shake the flask after each addition. When the colour changes to greenish blue, add 4 drops of iron(II)-1,1 O-phenanthroline solution (4,7). (Another appropriate coloured indicator may be used, at the discretion of the operator, see note.) Continue the addition of the ammonium iron(II) sulfate solution (4.6) until the colour of the medium changes from greenish blue to brown. If the endpoint is passed, return to it precisely by adding potassium permanganate solution (4.5). Deduct, from the volume of the ammonium iron(H) sulfate solution used, one-tenth of the volume of potassium permanganate solution added. Let V2 be the volume remaining after this deduction, which represents the exact volume of ammonium iron(II) sulfate solution equivalent to the excess potassium bichromate.

NOTE -- The titration of the excess of bichromate with the solution of ammonium iron(n) sulfate (4.6) can also be carried out in the presence of a mixture of

10 Repeatability
The absolute difference between two independent single test results, obtained using the same method on identical test material in the same laboratory by the same operator using the same equipment within a shorl interval of time, will in not more than 5 "A of cases be greater than 1 ?4. of the arithmetic mean of the two results.

11 Test report
The test report shall specify:

-- -- -- --

all information

necessa~

for the complete identification

of the sample;

the sampling method used, if known; the test method used, together with reference to this International Standard;

all operating details not specified in this International Standard, or regarded as optional, together with details of any incidents which may have influenced the test result(s); the test result(s) obtained; if the repeatability has been checked, the final quoted result obtained.

Annex A
(normative)

Modified procedure for products containing essential oils

In the presence of essential oils, the distillate is turbid, with drops of essential cases the procedure shall be modified as follows.

oil floating on the surface.

In such

Collect the distillate in a 100 ml volumetric flask and allow it to stand for 2 h. Dilute to the mark with water, the interface between the two phases (essential oil and water) being at the level of the mark. Allow to stand for a further" 1 h to 2 h. Discard the small quantity of essential oil collected on the surface, either by suction with a fine pipette or by filtration through paper in a covered funnel. Transfer the still-turbid filtrate to a 150 ml flask and add 10 g of polystyrene Shake the stoppered flask for 15 mirr and then filter the mixture through should then have become clear and have lost its odour almost completely. Proceed with the determination on this liquid. granules (granule size 1 mm to 2 mm). gauze in a covered funnel. The liquid
